title: $Hi-PNG:$ Efficient Interval-Filtering ANNS via Hierarchical Interval Partition Navigating Graph

problem.claim: Existing approximate nearest neighbor search is extended to interval-filtering ANNS, where base and query vectors have numerical intervals and retrieved neighbors must have intervals fully contained within the query interval.

gap.claim: Real-world applications requiring numerical interval constraints create a retrieval setting that standard ANNS does not directly address efficiently.

contributions.claim: Defines interval-filtering approximate nearest neighbor search as a general retrieval task with interval containment constraints.
Introduces Hi-PNG, a hierarchical interval-partitioning navigating graph framework for locating the relevant search space while avoiding unnecessary computations.
Provides a theoretical analysis of the search space for the proposed approach.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper explicitly characterizes interval-filtering ANNS as a novel yet general retrieval task and presents Hi-PNG as its proposed framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on eight datasets, including benchmarks and real-world stock price data, report that Hi-PNG outperforms four state-of-the-art graph-based ANNS baselines.
The authors report up to 15× acceleration while maintaining high precision.
The authors report that all code and data generation are available in the linked repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: ANNS retrieves similar vectors from high-dimensional data and is used in many applications.
Some applications additionally require numerical interval filtering, with valid neighbors fully contained within the query interval.
Hi-PNG hierarchically partitions interval space to identify the search space efficiently and reduce unnecessary computation.
The paper analyzes the search space theoretically.
Experiments across eight datasets compare Hi-PNG with four graph-based ANNS baselines and report speed and precision results.

source_observation.claim: Hierarchically partitioning a numerical constraint space can help narrow graph-based nearest-neighbor search.

interpretation.claim: Constraint-aware indexing may reduce unnecessary distance computations when retrieval requires both similarity and interval containment.

application.claim: For vector retrieval with numerical-range constraints, consider combining graph navigation with hierarchical partitioning of the constraint domain.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how performance changes for constraint distributions, interval dimensionality, or workloads outside the reported datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, hardware, query workloads, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not provide precision values, latency definitions, or baseline configuration details.
The abstract does not state the theoretical assumptions or guarantees.
The abstract does not describe the Hi-PNG algorithm's construction and query procedures in detail.
